previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: James, a 60-year-old man with a history of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, alcohol use disorder, and tobacco use, was admitted after being found unresponsive in a coffee shop with hypoxia and signs of acute alcohol intoxication. He received intravenous fluids for hypernatremia, a dose of methylprednisolone for COPD exacerbation, and azithromycin for infection prophylaxis. Despite medical recommendations, he refused further treatment, including medications for alcohol withdrawal and morning lab work, and left the hospital against medical advice on the morning of hospital day one.
problems: Acute alcoholic intoxication in alcoholism, continuous

Brief Hospital Course:
The patient is a ___ year old man with COPD and a long history of 
alcohol abuse and multiple visits to ___ who presented with 
worsening dyspnea and subjective fever.

# Dyspnea: Patient with untreated COPD (noncompliant with all 
home meds). Prelim CXR also shows bilateral opacities 
(atelectasis/scarring vs multifocal pneumonia). Given patient's 
alcoholism and poor dentition, significant concern for 
aspiration and anaerobic organisms. Started on prednisone for 
COPD exacerbation and given nebs as needed. Also treated with 
levofloxacin (to cover for CAP) and metronidazole (given 
aspiration risk). Patient got 4 days of antibiotics before 
eloping. We were not able to give him outpatient prescriptions 
for inhalers or antibiotics before he left.

# Alcohol withdrawal: Patient with increased tremulousness and 
agitation as well as hypertension and tachycardia consistent 
with alcohol withdrawal. Initially scoring in the high ___ on 
the CIWA scale. Placed on diazepam 10mg for CIWA>10.

# Hypertension: Patient persistantly hypertensive to 170s, 
attributed primarily to withdrawal (as also tremulous and 
tachycardic). He was started on amlodipine 5mg daily, as he had 
been discharged on this previously, but primary focus was 
treating withdrawal.
